spec: W23b FAIL-13 run_context: the cross-language test vectors. The Python SDK (client/run_context.py), the CLI (cli/testlookup_cli/run_context.py) and the server (schemas.RunContext + run_context_service) all run these cases; the Java / JS / Go SDKs adopt this file when they send run_context. The allowlists, caps, patterns and token shapes below are pinned equal to backend/app/services/run_context_vocab.py by backend/tests/test_bisect_drift_vocab_parity.py. Grow it (new cases, new keys); never rewrite a case.
conventions: cases[].files: path (relative to the root) -> text. Write each as the UTF-8 bytes of the text EXACTLY as given (a \r\n stays \r\n), creating parent directories; a lockfile is hashed as raw bytes (sha256, lower-case hex). Only LOCKFILE_NAMES directly in the root are read: no directory walk, no glob.
cases[].env: the ONLY variables set for the case: every ENV_ALLOWLIST key and every TESTLOOKUP_* variable not listed is unset first.

cases[].expect: the exact run_context the SDK builds (sections with keys in any order; an empty section is omitted) AND the exact object the server accepts UNCHANGED and stores. Detected runtime keys are not part of it: an SDK removes from its built runtime every key in its detected_runtime_keys list that expect.runtime does not name (expect.runtime keys come from TESTLOOKUP_RUNTIME, which wins over detection), and treats a runtime left empty as absent.

TESTLOOKUP_RUNTIME / TESTLOOKUP_IMAGE_DIGESTS: comma-separated key=value entries, split on the first '=', surrounding whitespace stripped; an entry failing patterns.runtime_key / patterns.version (or patterns.image_name / patterns.digest) is dropped, never sent.

env values (SDK): control characters removed, truncated to caps.env_value characters, then the userinfo_rule, then any token_shapes match replaces the WHOLE value with redacted. The server re-applies every rule: token_shapes on the value as sent, the userinfo rule, redaction_service.redact_text (credential and PII shapes), then token_shapes again (see redactions). Runtime versions, hashes, image names and digests are never redacted: they are pattern-checked, and a value failing its pattern is refused, never cleaned.

caps.bytes: len(json.dumps(run_context, separators=(',', ':')).encode('utf-8')) with non-ASCII escaped as \uXXXX (Python's default); over it the SDK drops env, then image_digests, then runtime extras until it fits; the server refuses it (too_large).

refusals[]: run_context bodies the server refuses with a 422 on every route: loc ends with field, the message is the sentence (JSON routes: FastAPI's msg is 'Value error, ' + message; /ingest/file: detail {code: 'invalid_run_context', message}). No SDK ever builds one.
redactions[]: raw env values an old or foreign client might send, and the value the server stores.
form_refusals[]: /ingest/file form values that are not a JSON object: 422 detail {code, message}.

cases.name: two-lockfiles-lf
cases.about: Two lockfiles at the root, LF text, hashed as raw bytes; the runtime comes from TESTLOOKUP_RUNTIME.

cases.name: env-outside-allowlist-dropped
cases.about: Only ENV_ALLOWLIST keys are sent; any other variable is dropped by the SDK (the server would 422 it).

cases.name: userinfo-redacted
cases.about: A ://user:password@ value keeps the user and loses the password (the SDK's userinfo rule == redact_text's).

cases.name: over-long-value-truncated
cases.about: A value over 200 characters is TRUNCATED to 200 by the SDK (the server would 422 it).

redactions.name: token-shapes
redactions.about: The server re-applies TOKEN_SHAPES (on the value as sent, and again after the other rules): a value an old or foreign SDK sent raw is stored as [REDACTED], whole.

redactions.name: bearer
redactions.about: redact_text's Bearer rule (the SDK does not apply it: no 40+ character run).

redactions.name: jwt
redactions.about: redact_text's JWT rule (three dotted segments; the SDK does not apply it).

redactions.name: token-assignment
redactions.about: redact_text's token= rule (the SDK does not apply it).

redactions.name: pii-shapes
redactions.about: redact_text also applies its PII shapes to env values (an address, a dotted quad): send a label, not a host.
